name: Cons & Cover-ups
sub: Scammers, frauds and the people who caught them

intros.e094: We start with a phone call most of us hang up on. Alex Goldman stays on the line with a tech-support scammer, then follows the trail all the way to India.
intros.e093: Next, a con man in Orange County and the family he nearly destroyed. This one topped the charts for weeks and turned into a TV series.
intros.e113: Someone keeps hijacking a teenager's Snapchat account. Reply All goes looking for who, and how.
intros.e010: Now a rare thing: a show retracting its own story. This American Life spends a full hour on how it got Mike Daisey's Apple factory account wrong.
intros.e164: From the Theranos saga, the final chapter. Elizabeth Holmes and Sunny Balwani get their sentences.
intros.e202: And we close with the investigation that won a Pulitzer. Pablo Torre follows the money behind a no-show deal for Kawhi Leonard.

name: Little Mysteries
sub: Small puzzles, chased all the way down

intros.e063: Starlee Kine finds a belt buckle and decides to find its owner. Some critics have called this the best podcast episode ever made.
intros.e075: Jonathan Goldstein helps a friend try to get back some CDs he lent to Moby, years before Moby got famous.
intros.e130: A man remembers a nineties song that no one else can find. Not on the internet, not anywhere. Reply All goes hunting.
intros.e064: Another case from Mystery Show, this one hinging on a single photo of Britney Spears.
intros.e092: Finally, the fitness icon who vanished from public life. Dan Taberski goes looking for Richard Simmons.

intros.e049: This is where the modern podcast boom began. Episode one of Serial, and the case of Adnan Syed.
intros.e076: In the Dark reopens the Jacob Wetterling case and asks why the sheriff's office never solved it.
intros.e006: A New York police officer secretly records his own precinct. What he captured is about quotas.
intros.e066: A license plate mix-up, a traffic stop, and everything that went wrong after it.
intros.e112: Reply All on the numbers system that drove New York policing, and what it did to the officers inside it.
intros.e077: A young woman reports a rape and the police don't believe her. This story later became the Netflix series Unbelievable.
intros.e119: In the Dark's second season opens with Curtis Flowers, a man tried six times for the same crime. This reporting fed into a Supreme Court case.
intros.e159: And a bookend: eight years after it all started, Serial returns for the day Adnan Syed walks out of court.

intros.e024: A short one to start. Who designs the sounds your devices make, and why they sound the way they do.
intros.e025: Kowloon Walled City, the densest, most lawless neighborhood on earth, and what it looked like from inside.
intros.e055: A Manhattan skyscraper with a hidden flaw, and the engineers who fixed it before anyone found out.
intros.e022: Why do ancient texts barely mention the color blue? Radiolab goes looking.
intros.e088: The Army Corps of Engineers once built a scale model of the entire Mississippi River basin. Here's what happened to it.
intros.e107: You used to be able to buy a house from the Sears catalog. It came in the mail.
intros.e020: A man reaches adulthood without any language at all, and what that tells us about how words shape thought.
intros.e106: And to close, how punk fashion went from homemade rebellion to something you could buy at the mall.

intros.e086: Karina Longworth opens her Joan Crawford series, by way of Douglas Fairbanks.
intros.e079: You get a car! An oral history of the most famous giveaway in daytime television.
intros.e116: Back to Longworth, fact-checking the legends around Hollywood's censorship czar.
intros.e082: The day Beyonce dropped Formation, recorded while it was all still happening.
intros.e134: Polly Platt helped make some of the great films of the seventies, and almost nobody knew her name.
intros.e140: A look back at America's Next Top Model, with someone who was there.
intros.e129: The Disney film the company would rather you forgot, and why.
intros.e201: And to finish, a record breaker: Taylor Swift announces an album on her boyfriend's podcast.

name: The Campaign Trail
sub: When candidates sat down with podcasters

intros.e056: We start in 2015, when a sitting president sat down in Marc Maron's garage.
intros.e068: Later that year, BuzzFeed's Another Round gets Hillary Clinton talking about race and reparations.
intros.e122: In 2019, a long-shot candidate named Andrew Yang makes his pitch for a universal basic income on Joe Rogan.
intros.e124: A few months later, Bernie Sanders on the same show, and a remark from Rogan that the campaign made the most of.
intros.e186: Jump to 2024. Donald Trump talks with Lex Fridman, one of the first stops on his podcast tour.
intros.e189: Kamala Harris on Call Her Daddy, a show built for young women, weeks before the election.
intros.e187: Trump and Theo Von, a freewheeling conversation that sent the show to number one.
intros.e190: Then three hours with Joe Rogan, days before the vote.
intros.e191: After the result, Jon Stewart and historian Heather Cox Richardson on what comes next.
intros.e197: And in 2025, Gavin Newsom launches his podcast with a guest few expected: Charlie Kirk.
